en: A general concept of the Anfangsgründe before us will best emerge and justify itself after the presentation of the contents.

The negotiations about a doctrine, whether one professes or doubts or rejects it, can, so the author thinks in the preface, properly be conducted with decorum and in peace. - With regard to the former, one sees from the conclusion of the preface that the author gives it a wide scope; as for the latter, the reviewer will not be able to negotiate with these Anfangsgründe without discord.
zh: 对眼前这部《思辨的哲学初阶》的一般概念，最好在陈述了内容之后才得出来，并由此得到辩护。
关于一种学说的争论——不管人们是承认它、怀疑它还是抛弃它——，作者先生在序言里认为，尽可以体面地、平和地进行。——就前者说，从序言的结尾可以看出，作者给了它一个很宽的范围；至于后者，书评人与这部《思辨的哲学初阶》打交道，是不能没有不和的。

en: The external form of this textbook the author defines in the preface as this: that it should simply be a textbook wholly and entirely according to the sceptical method.
In the whole course of the development the author takes care above all to go only so far as the sceptic could allow, - until finally scepticism is formally refuted in § 384.

The author has remained true to this intention in part and untrue in part, - untrue in so far as, on the ground that doubting is itself a thinking, he builds up the whole system of the laws of thought, as logic, and no less the whole system of the transcendental laws of representation (i.e. the Kantian Critique of Reason in extract), whereas the consistent sceptic denies the concept of a law altogether, - true in so far as the author keeps the whole within the sphere of a meagreness with which the sceptic cannot consider it worth his while to occupy himself at all; - certainly the most forceful manner of driving him off.
Why then did the author not begin at once with that late refutation of the sceptic?

Thus the problematic and provisional philosophizing that runs through several hundred paragraphs, as the author calls it, could have been spared; one understands the necessity, and thereby the relative value, of provisional governments, provisional decisions in the courts, etc., but what sense would a provisional philosophizing have?

With that refutation of scepticism in § 430 one could all the more begin, since, if the sceptic seizes the one side of the dilemma laid before him, it is declared that we can do nothing further than let him contradict himself from the first word he speaks; - or, if he takes up the other side, he is asked how the concept of reality could come into the understanding even only sceptically, and is then referred to an argumentation in which it is asserted that a determinate being also underlies the concepts and representations; but this determinate being of the representations and concepts, which the sceptic does not doubt, we think only as an improper determinate being, and, indubitably together with the concept of determinate being, [we think] something that is the principle of the representations and the ground of their possibility, a reality that the understanding must presuppose. - This refutation consists in nothing other than the positive assertion of what the sceptic negates, - if it is taken more thoroughly, in the insight that scepticism is actually irrefutable.

Nothing prevented beginning the whole speculative philosophy with that so-called refutation, which takes refuge in an absolute presupposition, or with this insight, laying aside all regard for the sceptic and philosophizing at once apodictically instead of provisionally.

In this provisional philosophizing, which is no philosophizing, consists the so-called sceptical method, which, highly pathetically recommended in § 22, as Herr Bouterwek calls it, is practically illustrated: "let neither pride nor admiration nor any other passion in your soul speak a word for any fundamental proposition! - If you think every proposition that another expects you to acknowledge as true as at the outset perhaps erroneous, then you are in the state of pure scepticism, and only in this state are you sure not to miss the standpoint of pure truth!"

On S. 12 it is said that we are rightly all the more mistrustful of disputed systems the more they bear witness to the rare talents of their authors and nevertheless have not drawn all good heads to their side.

To a cento of Kantian or his own formalities, which is supposed to give the sceptic no opening, the presentation of the system of some rare head, or even that against which the author warns on S. 11, would have been preferable, namely "to pay no attention at all to the sceptic and to adhere to a blind but very consistent dogmatism".
Consistent (I say, consistent) dogmatisms are indeed not very many, and to set up such a one is quite a different work from philosophizing in a provisional manner.
zh: 这部教科书的外在形式，作者在序言里这样规定：它应当干脆就是一部完全按照怀疑论方法的教科书。
在整个展开过程中，作者特别留意只走到怀疑论者所能容许的那一步为止，——直到怀疑论终于在 § 384 里被正式驳倒。
作者对这个打算一部分没有守住，一部分守住了，——没有守住在于：他以“怀疑本身也是一种思维”为根据，把整个思维规律的系统当作逻辑建立起来，同样也把整个先验的表象规律的系统（即康德《理性批判》的摘编）建立起来，而一贯的怀疑论者其实根本否认规律这个概念；——守住在于：作者把整个东西保持在一种贫乏的范围内，怀疑论者根本不值得费神去理会这种贫乏；——这倒确实是把怀疑论者赶走的最有劲的办法。
作者为什么不一上来就从那个迟到的对怀疑论者的反驳开始呢？
这样一来，那种贯穿好几百节的问题式的、临时的哲学思考——作者是这样称呼它的——本来就可以省掉；人们懂得临时政府的必然性，从而也懂得法庭上临时裁决之类东西的相对价值，但一种临时的哲学思考又有什么意义呢？

从 § 430 那个对怀疑论的驳斥开始，本来就更加说得过去，因为，如果怀疑论者抓住摆在他面前的两难的一边，那么要说明的就是：我们不能再做什么，只能让他从说出的第一个字开始就自相矛盾；——或者，如果他接下另一边，那么人们就问他，实在性这个概念哪怕只是怀疑地来说又怎么会进入知性，然后把他引向一种论证，这种论证主张：概念和表象也有一种定在作为基础；但是表象和概念这种定在——怀疑论者并不怀疑它——我们只把它想成一种不本真的定在，并且跟定在的概念一起不可怀疑地想成：有某种东西是表象的原则、是表象可能性的根据，是一种知性必须预设的实在性。——这个反驳不外乎是对怀疑论者所否定的东西作出正面的主张，——如果更彻底地来看，不外乎是洞见到：怀疑论其实是驳不倒的。
本来没有什么妨碍人们从那个所谓的反驳——它逃到一种绝对的预设里去了——或者从这种洞见出发，来开始整个思辨的哲学，把对怀疑论者的一切顾虑都撇在一边，并且立刻不作临时的哲学思考，而作无可置疑的哲学思考。
所谓的怀疑论方法，就存在于这种不是哲学思考的临时哲学思考里；这种方法在 § 22 里被非常动情地吹捧过，而且按布特维克先生的说法，还从实践上讲解得明明白白：“不要让骄傲、惊叹或你灵魂里的任何别的激情为任何根本命题说话！——如果你把别人要你承认为真的每一个命题，一开始都看成也许是错的，那你就处在纯粹怀疑的状态里，只有在这种状态里你才靠得住，不会错过纯粹真理的立足点！”
S. 12 上说：我们对有争议的体系越是心存戒备就越是有道理，因为它们越是显出作者具有罕见的才能，却偏偏没能把所有聪明的头脑都拉到它们一边。
比起一堆康德式的或他自己的形式套话——这种东西不该给怀疑论者留下任何破绽——，本来更可取的是把某个罕见头脑的体系陈述出来，或者甚至是作者在 S. 11 上警告的那件事，即“根本不理会怀疑论者，去抱住一种盲目的、但非常一贯的独断论”。
一贯的（我说的是，一贯的）独断论其实并不多，而建立起这样一种独断论，跟以临时的方式作哲学思考完全是两码事。

en: The introduction treats, in 60 paragraphs, I. of philosophy in general, II. of the relation of philosophy to erudition, III. of the first and last object of all philosophical thinking, IV. of the division of philosophy, V. of the method of philosophical study; of the tone in which this introduction is written the first paragraph may serve as an example; it reads thus: "Among the sciences that have been found worthy of study by the brightest and best heads of every cultivated age, there is one that usually calls itself philosophy, in German sometimes with the curious name of world-wisdom."

In III. it is said that a science which rejects all presuppositions and therefore may place no proposition at the head of the propositions following upon it as a ground of proof without proof, could begin with nothing other than a summons to the thinking being to acknowledge itself as a thinking being through thinking itself; - one gains the hope that the author has through this demand of intellectual intuition won a firm point from which he will construct consciousness; but after it has also been remarked in § 39 that in the acknowledgement of ourselves there lies the relation of ourselves to something outside us, which we find in us, insofar as we cognize it, § 40 raises the question: "With which proposition shall we continue to philosophize, after we have thought ourselves as merely thinking in general, but otherwise as utterly unacquainted with ourselves?"

Since the author has no answer to this question and does not know how he should continue, the method occurs to him in § 41 'to make it as comfortable for himself as the philosophers have done long enough, namely to begin by enumerating a series of so-called powers of the soul'; but, he asks, what then entitles us to this enumeration?

If one then finds in addition that the list comes out differently in every school, that the dispute about the effects of these powers is often an empty dispute about words, to which only the indeterminacy and the difference of languages has given occasion, then we are rightly mistrustful of all such lists; after the same thing has been said over and above in § 42, and it has been remarked that even the presupposed ground of division is first attempted to be demonstrated after the presupposition of the divisions, and that with such a procedure it is impossible to ground any system as philosophy, a beginning is nevertheless made with some system of powers of the soul and it is tried how far one gets with it.

However insignificant those grounds are, they would still have sufficed to keep psychology off one's back; the ground why a beginning is nevertheless made with it is given verbatim in § 43 as follows: "Since, however, philosophical speculation has always taken this course, it must surely be the most natural one." - It is also said to be necessary both for the understanding of the most famous philosophies and for the transition from the popular to the philosophical manner of representation. - After this welcome discovery of a psychological entry into philosophy, both a psychological division of philosophy, § 44, and psychological presuppositions are permitted, § 46, according to which we distinguish certain directions of attention to ourselves from others, insofar as these distinctions are (a) certain through themselves, (b) asserted by common human understanding as much as (c) approved by all philosophizing schools, § 48.

Since now doubts are also thoughts, and we, even when we doubt, follow some rule as a necessary relation of our thoughts to one another, we gain through the separation of this relation the concept of logic.

"How (§ 49), however, mere thinking, which also includes doubt in itself, is different from the knowledge that excludes doubt, about that not even two philosophical schools are yet agreed." - The problematic science of the grounding of all parts of philosophical knowledge [is] elementary doctrine or metaphysics. - According to this psychological division, which is an example of the author's problematic and sceptical method, these Anfangsgründe of speculative philosophy fall into three main parts, with many highly methodical subdivisions.
We shall give only a few samples from the first two parts and keep chiefly to the third.
zh: 导论用 60 节讲了：I. 一般意义上的哲学，II. 哲学与博学的关系，III. 一切哲学思维最初和最后的对象，IV. 哲学的分类，V. 哲学研究的方法；至于这篇导论是用什么调子写的，第一节可以作个例子，它是这样说的：“在每一个有教养的时代最明亮、最优秀的头脑认为值得研究的各门科学中，有一门通常自称为哲学，在德语里有时还带着‘世界智慧’这个古怪的名字。”

在 III. 里说，一门抛弃一切预设、因而完全不允许把任何命题不经证明就当作证明根据放在它后面那些命题之前的科学，只能以向思维着的东西提出这样一种要求开头：要求它作为思维着的东西通过思维本身承认自己；——于是人们生出希望，以为作者凭这个对智性直观的要求赢得了一个牢固的立足点，可以从这里建构意识；可是，在 § 39 里又指出，在承认我们自己的时候，已经包含着我们自己与我们身外的某种东西的关系，这种东西我们在自己身上找到，只要我们认识它；随后 § 40 又提出这个问题：“在我们把自己一般只当作思维着的、此外则完全认作对自己毫无所知之后，我们该用哪个命题继续作哲学思考？”
由于作者对这个问题没有答案，也不知道该怎么往下走，他就在 § 41 里想到了这个办法：‘把事情弄得舒服些，像哲学家们早就弄得够舒服的那样，也就是从列举一串所谓的灵魂能力开始’；但是他问，究竟什么给了我们权利去作这种列举呢？
如果人们还发现，这份目录在每个学派里都各不相同，关于这些能力的作用的争论往往只是一场空洞的字面之争，其起因不过是语言的不确定和差异，那么我们就有理由对所有这类目录心存疑虑；在 § 42 里又多此一举地说了同样的话，还指出：被预设的分类根据，也要先预设了各个门类之后才试图去证明，而用这样的做法，根本不可能把任何一个体系当作哲学来奠基；尽管如此，人们还是从某个灵魂能力的体系开始，试试看这样能走多远。

那些根据虽然无足轻重，本来也足够把心理学挡在门外了；可终究还是从它开始，这理由在 § 43 里一字不差地这样给出：“不过，既然哲学思辨一直走的是这条路，它大概也就是最自然的路。”——还说，这对理解那些最著名的哲学、对从流行的表象方式过渡到哲学的表象方式，都是必要的。——自从发现了这条通往哲学的心理学入口——这是件受欢迎的事——，人们就既允许对哲学作心理学的分类（§ 44），也允许心理学的预设（§ 46）；按照这些预设，我们把某些对自身的注意方向跟别的方向区分开来，只要这些区分 (a) 是自身确定的，(b) 既由普通人的常识所主张，(c) 又得到一切哲学学派的赞同（§ 48）。
因为怀疑也是思想，而且我们即使在怀疑时也遵循着某种规则，把它当作我们思想彼此之间的一种必然关系，所以我们通过把这个关系分离出来，就得到了逻辑的概念。
“然而（§ 49），包含怀疑在内的单纯思维，跟排除怀疑的知识究竟有什么不同，对此连两个哲学学派都还没有取得一致。”——给哲学知识的各个部分作论证的问题式的科学，就是基础学说或形而上学。——按照这种心理学的划分——它是作者那种问题式的、怀疑论的方法的一个例子——，这部思辨的哲学初阶分成三个主要部分，还带着许多极其讲究方法的下属划分。
对前两个部分，我们只举很少几个样品，主要讲第三个部分。

en: In the propaedeutic psychology, after the rejection of the assertion of a soul-thing, the usual three concepts — subject, object and representation — are given as the basic conditions of the concept of self-observation; provisionally, sensibility and reason are opposed according to self-observation, both are treated psychologically, and the usual stuff about higher and lower soul-powers is brought in; by the fact that everything is to be set up only provisionally and as it is observed, the author has freed himself from all demands of a construction of this manifoldness of the faculties; it passes from one to the other in the following ways, § 80.

Since we are further conscious of a faculty of bringing vanished impressions back to consciousness, even though this does not always succeed, we first designate it by the name of the faculty of recollection and secondly infer another faculty in which the representations rest, as it were, when they have vanished from consciousness — memory (which is thus the faculty of the faculty of recollection — not even the common distinction between memory and the faculty of recollection is correctly given), § 81.
Closely related to recollection, but yet different from it, is the imagination, etc.
From § 92 one already sees provisionally what is to be expected of the logic; 'the question: whence the laws or necessary conditions of thinking? remains here (in psychology) still unanswered.
It will also probably always remain unanswered.'
zh: 在入门心理学里，驳回了关于一个灵魂之物的主张之后，作为自我观察这一概念的基本条件，给出了通常的三个概念：主体、客体和表象；暂时地，按自我观察把感性和理性对立起来，两者都从心理学上加以处理，又搬来关于高级和低级灵魂能力的通常说法；由于一切都只是暂时地、并且照它被观察到的样子被摆出来，作者就摆脱了对这种能力杂多作建构的一切要求；它以下面这些方式从一个过渡到另一个，§ 80。
其次，既然我们意识到有一种能力，能把消逝了的印象重新带进意识，尽管这件事并不总是成功，我们首先就用回想能力这个名称来指它，其次又推断出另一种能力，表象从意识中消逝之后仿佛就安息在其中，——即记忆（所以记忆就是回想能力的能力，——就连记忆与回想能力之间通常的区别也没有正确地给出），§ 81。
与回想近亲、但又与之有别的是想象力，等等。
从 § 92 已经可以预先看出，对逻辑学能指望什么；“思维的各种规律或必然条件是从哪里来的？这个问题在这里（在心理学里）仍然没有得到回答。
它大概也永远会得不到回答。”

en: In the logic, the distinction of concepts, judgements and inferences is grounded on the following justification.

§ 135 b. 'In most schools one regards the concepts as products of the understanding in the narrower sense, the propositions as products of the power of judgement and the inferences as products of reason in the narrower sense; but since on the path of our speculation we have come to know reason only as the thinking principle as such (the author here refers to a paragraph of the psychology, and is thus really able to regard that psychological proceeding provisionally as speculation), and have found no occasion to assume a special faculty of the power of judgement, we for the present hold only to the concept of synthesis as such; in accordance with this, it depends only on us to become conscious of the concepts, propositions and inferences, as they are distinguished in common life, as different representations that are possible only through synthesis.'

On p. 57 we learn that language coincides with the understanding; as soon as we relate the latter to something and recognize this as something separated from it through marks, we need a sensible representation in order to fasten the concept to it in memory as to a second mark; this mark is called word.

On p. 67 we learn that in the Kantian school the connection of concepts into propositions is called pure synthesis or synthesis a priori. - According to § 182, p. 88, the condition of a proposition is that two concepts are related to each other through a third concept; this third concept is what the logicians call the copula and signifies thinking itself; - but precisely because the copula signifies thinking itself as activity, it is not a concept in the proposition itself; as it is present, insofar as one reflects on it, insofar as it is thus made into a concept, it is not present in the proposition; the relation in the proposition does not happen through a third concept, this is the inference. - Rich in such indeterminacies or in such deep disclosures as the above one about language, the definitions of the manifold kinds of concepts, propositions and inferences run on through the logic along the mostly ordinary Kantian moments, with a very methodical appearance of divisions.
zh: 在逻辑学里，概念、判断和推理之间的区分，是以下面这一番辩护为依据的。

§ 135 b。“在大多数学派那里，人们把概念看作狭义的知性的产物，把命题看作判断力的产物，把推理看作狭义的理性的产物；可是，既然我们在思辨的道路上只认识到理性是一般思维原则（作者在这里引到心理学的一节，因此能把那种心理学的暂时做法现实地看作思辨），又还没有找到理由去假定一种特殊的判断力能力，我们就暂且只守住一般综合这一概念；按照这个概念，我们能否把概念、命题和推理——就像人们在日常生活里区分它们那样——作为只有通过综合才可能的各不相同的表象而意识到，就只取决于我们自己。”
S. 57 上我们得知，语言与知性是重合的；我们一旦把知性与某物相关联，并把该物作为与知性分离的东西而通过标记来承认，我们就需要一种感性的表象，以便把概念当作记忆中的第二个标记系在它上面；这个标记就叫做词。

S. 67 上我们得知，在康德学派那里，把概念联结成命题叫做纯粹综合或 a priori［先验］综合。——按照 § 182、S. 88，一个命题的条件是两个概念通过第三个概念而相互关联；这第三个概念就是逻辑学家所谓的系词，它意味着思维本身；——但正因为系词意味着作为活动的思维本身，它就不是命题本身中的一个概念；它作为被反思到的东西、因而被造成概念的东西而存在时，并不存在于命题之中；命题中的关联不是通过第三个概念发生的，这就是推理。——逻辑学里那些关于各种概念、命题和推理的定义，依着康德那些多半很通常的环节，带着一副很有方法的划分外观一路延续下去，其中满是这类不确定，或者满是像上面关于语言那样的深刻揭示。

en: The third part.

The elementary philosophy is begun, after an introduction, with a doctrine of doubt, which, since it does not construct scepticism from the highest standpoint, which is still always being shifted, is formal and without scientific interest.

One hopes that the second part of the elementary philosophy, the doctrine of knowledge, will now finally go to knowledge itself and to truth, but one finds oneself deceived again; it is 'begun with a theory of the general laws and human representations, in order to agree with the sceptic for the present about the scope and the system of these laws'; as the ground of this it is stated: because in the meantime it could do no harm.

This transcendental theory is then nothing further than the hackneyed Kantian expositions of space and time and of the categories, which through their endless repetitions in all textbooks have become utterly disgusting.

Does the author then seriously believe that the sceptic will put up with these transcendental laws of representations? - In the logic one had to hope that a transcendental deduction would after all be given in the elementary philosophy for the forms that serve to divide concepts and propositions; but the author takes everything just as it is found in Kant, and believes that one must let the table of categories set up by the author of the critique of reason pass as complete, as long as one can raise nothing with ground against the asserted completeness.

He moreover 'ascribes to the assertion of this completeness only the value of psychological truth, so long as the distinction both of the mathematical and the dynamical in our knowledge and of the subjective and the objective is not explained to the complete satisfaction of reason'.
Why then has the author not treated the categories, like the whole logic, only after this distinction grounded by reason, whereby he would have prepared for himself the possibility of deducing them?

But in the following paragraph we hear that 'fortunately so much does not depend on the outcome of the dispute about the completeness and thoroughness of the Kantian table of categories; since the understanding never cognizes an object with it, there may always be more or fewer categories'.
One may well believe that in the bottom of their hearts most Kantians too care nothing about a couple of categories more or less, but it has not easily been admitted so openly.

Since the author has once arrived at the good feeling that a couple of categories more or less do not matter to the cause of philosophy, since through them we do not cognize the objects as they are, and thus do not come to truth through them, - for what has the author [then] seen fit to set up such a propaedeutic psychology, such a series of formal logical definitions, which matter even less?
No ground is to be seen except that the better feeling, which is not in earnest about all these indifferent matters, has let itself be overmastered by the traditional custom.
If the author, moreover (in III.

On the transcendental connection of reason and sensibility) definitively recognizes the critical philosophy as a system of transcendental representations, i.e. as an empty 'formalism', then the author had all the more to leave lying aside the trivialities of the logic and the emptiness of what he calls transcendental knowledge, if he could not procure for it a real meaning through a construction from the highest standpoint. - In § 416, in the apodictic, these first grounds of philosophy come to a principle of philosophy, of which we have to give an account.

According to § 420 we are caught in the dilemma 'either to deny all meaning to the concept of reality, insofar as it is originally supposed to signify something other than reason itself, and to hold pure reason alone for the true reality, but the sensible representations for mediate products of pure reason; - or we must assert a real principle which, as different from reason as from sensibility, lies at the basis of both'; - here the author had partly before his eyes the Kantian concept of reason, according to which pure reason is absolutely opposed to sensibility, but partly he again confuses reason in the idealistic sense with that formal pure reason.

In the Kantian system, as it is ordinarily taken, the sensible representations are not products of reason; but if they are posited as such, then the concept of reality has meaning also for the products of reason, and indeed the highest.

In the next paragraph the author opposes to the first side of the dilemma, the self-production of reason in the idealistic system, according to which reason creates consciousness and objectivity, that 'thereby consciousness is leapt over, for in consciousness itself everything behaves in the opposite way, and the cognizing subject finds itself only in the relation to objects, but not as their producer'.
What is to be done against such a ground?
The author's real principle accordingly falls out thus: it is subject and object in original opposition.

Since the matter stands thus, the reviewer doubts whether the author will understand him when he says that philosophy is pursued solely in order to sublate the opposition of subject and object and the contradictions into which cognition [loses itself] when it takes that opposition as it is found in consciousness; this dissolution is indeed posited in an original opposing of a subject and an object, but in such a way that it is conditioned by an original being-identical of the two.

If the author means that through this identity idealism leaps over consciousness, the answer is that this identity is indeed in consciousness and is consciousness itself, but present unconsciously, as reason, which knows itself only in philosophizing itself.

With his original opposition of the power of judgement as real principle, the author now finds all riddles of psychology and logic solved; in the logic it would have had to remain unexplained and undecided whether the concepts, propositions have reality; the logic could not explain the object to which the representations etc. were related; through the real principle everything is now posited as real, the thoughts are a knowledge, thinking in itself presupposed the object, the real principle first states briefly and plainly that the objects have absolute reality.

One may light upon the good opinion that in the author's real principle the absolute identity of subject and object is really contained, if, as cited above, the real principle is supposed to lie at the basis of sensibility and reason, if further § 429 expresses the absolute real judgement as the self-assertion of the subject with an opposed object in one reality; but it soon becomes clear that this one reality is only a same reality, i.e. a concept or a substratum, not a living identity of the two.

Already at the beginning of these first grounds of this speculative philosophy we saw that the author, after he had taken up self-thinking as the starting point of philosophy in the manner of idealism, now did not know what he should continue with, and so took refuge in the natural path of psychology and logic, - paths that had to be scorned if the real principle is the absolute identity; one is fully enlightened when, from § 431 on, an absolute ideal principle is placed alongside that real principle, because (and yet the real principle was supposed to lie at the basis of reason and sensibility) the subjective possibility of the concepts also belongs to reasoning and is not explained by that real principle, - insofar as it rests on pure abstraction; and according to § 434 it is impossible not only to explain reality from reason or reason from reality, but also to explain both as absolutely one and the same.
zh: 第三部分。
入门哲学在导论之后以一门怀疑学说开头，这门学说既然不是从最高立足点出发来建构怀疑论——而那个立足点还一再被推移——，它就是形式的，没有科学旨趣。
人们希望，入门哲学的第二部分，即知识学说，现在终于会去谈知识本身和真理，可是发现自己又受了骗；它“以一门关于一般规律和人的表象的理论开头，以便先与怀疑论者就这些规律的范围和体系达成一致”；为此给出的理由是：因为在这期间这不会有什么害处。
这种先验理论无非就是康德关于空间、时间和范畴的那些被嚼烂了的阐述，它们在所有教科书里被无限重复，已经变得完全令人作呕。
作者难道当真相信，怀疑论者会容忍这些关于表象的先验规律？——在逻辑学里人们本来应当希望，那些用来划分概念和命题的形式，在入门哲学里终究会得到一个先验演绎；可是作者把一切都照康德那里的样子直接拿过来，并且相信，只要人们不能有根据地反对所主张的完备性，就必须让《理性批判》的作者所提出的范畴表算作完备的。
此外他还“只把心理学真理的价值归给这一完备性的主张，只要我们的知识中数学的东西和力学的东西的区分、以及主观的东西和客观的东西的区分，还没有得到让理性完全满意的说明”。
那么，作者为什么不把范畴、乃至整个逻辑学，放到这个由理性建立起来的区分之后再来处理呢？这样他也就为自己准备好了演绎那些范畴的可能性。
可是在接下来的一节里我们听说，“幸好关于康德范畴表的完备性和彻底性的争论结果并没有那么要紧；既然知性凭它永远认识不到任何客体，那么范畴多几个或少几个都无妨”。
可以相信，大多数康德派在心底里也不在乎多几个或少几个范畴，只是这样公开承认却不容易见到。
既然作者一旦有了这种良好的感觉：多几个或少几个范畴对哲学的事业并不要紧，因为我们凭它们终究认识不到客体本来的样子，因而也凭它们达不到真理，——那么作者［又］何必去摆出这样一门入门心理学、这样一串更加不要紧的形式逻辑定义呢？
看不出有什么理由，只能说那种较好的感觉——它对所有这些无所谓的东西并不当真——让因袭的习俗给压过去了。
如果作者进一步（在 III.
论理性与感性的先验联结）明确认识到批判哲学是一个先验表象的体系，也就是一种空洞的“形式主义”，那么作者就更该把逻辑学里那些琐屑的东西、以及他所谓先验知识的空洞放在一边，既然他不能通过一种从最高立足点出发的建构给它弄出一个实在的意义来。——在 § 416 里，这些哲学的初始根据在确证学（Apodiktik）中归到一个哲学原则，对这个原则我们是要作出交代的。

按照 § 420，我们陷入两难，“要么否认实在性这一概念还有什么意义——只要它原初应当意味着理性本身之外的某种东西——，并把纯粹理性单独看作真正的实在性，而把感性表象看作纯粹理性的间接产物；——要么我们就必须主张一个实在原则，它既与理性有别，也与感性有别，是两者的根据”；——作者在这里一半盯着康德的理性概念，按这个概念，纯粹理性与感性绝对对立，另一半又把观念论意义上的理性与那种形式性的纯粹理性混在一起。
在康德体系中，也就是照通常的理解，感性表象并不是理性的产物；可是如果把它们设定为理性的产物，那么实在性这一概念对理性的产物也就有意义，而且是最高意义。
在下一节里，作者针对两难的第一面，即观念论体系中理性的自我生产——按这种说法，理性创造出意识和客观性——，提出反驳说，“这样一来意识就被跳过去了，因为在意识本身里一切都是反过来的，进行认识的主体只在与客体的关联中找到自己，而不是作为客体的生产者找到自己”。
面对这样一个根据，还能说什么呢？
照此看来，作者的实在原则就是这样：它是处于原初对立中的主体和客体。
事情既然如此，评论者就怀疑，作者是否懂得他这句话：哲学之所以被从事，完全只是为了扬弃主体与客体的对立，以及认识在把这种对立照它在意识中被发现的样子接受下来时［陷入］的那些矛盾；这一解决确实被设定为对一个主体和一个客体的原初对立设置，但却是以两者的原初同一存在为条件的。
如果作者认为，观念论通过这种同一性跳过了意识，那么回答是：这种同一性确实在意识之中，并且就是意识本身，但它是无意识地存在着的，作为理性，而理性只在哲学思考本身中认识自己。
凭他把判断力原初地对立起来作为实在原则，作者现在就发现心理学和逻辑学的一切谜团都解开了；在逻辑学里，概念、命题究竟有没有实在性，本来必然一直是未加解释、悬而未决的，逻辑学无法解释表象等等所关联的那个客体；通过实在原则，现在一切都设定为实在的，思想是一种知识，思维自在地以客体为前提，而实在原则干脆直说客体具有绝对的实在性。
人们可能生出这样一种善意看法：作者的实在原则里现实地包含着主体与客体的绝对同一性，如果像上面引述的那样，实在原则应当作为感性和理性的根据，又如果 § 429 把绝对的实在判断表达为主体与一个对立客体在一种实在性中的自我主张；但很快就清楚了，这一种实在性只是一种相同的实在性，也就是一个概念或一个基底，而不是两者的活生生的同一性。

在这门思辨哲学的这些初始根据的开头我们就已经看到，作者以观念论的方式把自我思维采纳为哲学的出发点之后，却不知道该接着做什么，于是逃到心理学和逻辑学这两条自然的路上去了，——如果实在原则就是绝对同一性，这两条路本来是该被鄙弃的；而当从 § 431 起，在那条实在原则旁边又摆出一个绝对的观念原则时，人们就彻底看明白了，因为（可实在原则本该是理性和感性的根据）概念的主观可能性也属于推想，并且没有由那条实在原则得到解释，——就它建立在纯粹抽象之上而言；而按照 § 434，不仅不可能从理性解释实在性、或从实在性解释理性，也不可能把两者解释为绝对同一的东西。

en: Once again, at § 438, the hope rises that the author will finally find his way out of dualism; here there is talk of the idea of the absolute; this highest of all concepts is supposed to mean both the real principle and the ideal principle.

If the author had made clear to himself what he said by this, he could not a few paragraphs earlier have declared it impossible to posit the ideal and real principle as one; for what does this doubled meaning of the absolute mean? how can the absolute mean both, if it is not at once real and ideal principle and if precisely thereby both are not one and the same?
Has the author forgotten that § 410 reproached the Kantians with making the absolute into a mere idea?

Why does he not put to himself the question that he puts to the sceptic in § 430: how does the idea of the absolute, as that which means both ideal and real principle, come into the understanding even only sceptically? - But the absolute serves the author for nothing further than to remark that through the concept of it, in its meaning as real principle, we think an objective, a closed whole or total, and that in its meaning as ideal principle it is the concept of the transcendentally infinite and thereby also of infinite doubt in thinking as in a never closed series of concepts.
zh: 在 § 438 那里，希望又一次升起来：作者终于会走出二元论；这里说的是绝对者的观念；这个一切概念中最高的概念，据说既意味着实在原则，又意味着观念原则。
如果作者曾弄清楚他这样说意味着什么，那么他在前面几节就不能宣布把观念原则和实在原则设定为一是不可能的；绝对者的这种双重含义究竟意味着什么？如果绝对者并不同时是实在原则和观念原则，如果正因如此两者并不是同一个东西，它又怎么可能意味着两者？
作者难道忘了，§ 410 曾责备康德派把绝对者弄成单纯的观念？

他为什么不把他在 § 430 向怀疑论者提出的那个问题提给自己：绝对者的观念，作为既意味着观念原则又意味着实在原则的东西，哪怕只是怀疑地，又是怎么进入知性的？——但绝对者在作者那里除了让人注意到下面这一点之外没有别的用处：我们通过绝对者的概念，在它作为实在原则的含义中，思考的是一个客观的、一个封闭的整体或总体，而它在作为观念原则的含义中，是先验无限者的概念，因而也是思维中作为一条永不封闭的概念系列的那种无限怀疑的概念。

en: If Kant has translated the common definition that the human being consists of body and soul into the one that he consists of reason and sensibility, then not much has been improved, but both state the opposition very clearly; Herr Bouterwek's translation into an ideal and a real principle, on the other hand, only confuses the matter further; his real principle already posits alongside the object a subject which, § 432, 'can reason, only not think in itself, although of course the schools take both for one'.

Alongside reason, as the ideal principle, and alongside the real principle, Herr Bouterwek nevertheless also needs sensibility in particular, for just as the real principle lies at the basis of reason so badly that one still needs a reason outside the real principle, so it will presumably not lie at the basis of sensibility any better; one finds clarification about this only further below.

The last section of this transcendental philosophy - on transcendental resignation, which begins with this, that with all philosophizing we cannot raise ourselves above the speculative opposition of the ideal and real principle - lists the riddles that remain over after all philosophizing; a) consciousness is to itself an insoluble riddle; b) the plurality and manifoldness of sensible representations is explained neither by the ideal nor by the real principle; the latter gives nothing but the object in general, not this or that object, § 446.

The former, § 447, is the I in thinking, as simple in opposition to manifoldness; we therefore need sensibility for the explanation of the same, § 448. c) With regard to the form of cognition and the Kantian laws of representation, § 451 leaves nothing over but to let them rest on their own altogether. - Given this impossibility of a transcendental satisfaction of reason, absolute truth is only an idea, and (§ 453) 'in the consciousness of the impossibility of finding it realized, we then help ourselves empirically with the concept of empirical or psychological truth, which we - think as an agreement of our representations with their objects!!'

Satis superque. - At the end there still follow the Kantian dispatchings of rational psychology, cosmology and theology; with the idea of God, § 462, Herr Bouterwek again recognizes only the antinomic character of the persistence of the opposition between reality and ideality and of its annihilation by pure thought; not that the synthesis of the all and the nothing must be absolute reality.
zh: 如果康德把“人由身体和灵魂构成”这个通常的定义译成了“人由理性和感性构成”，那并没有改善多少，但两者都把对立表达得很清楚；布特维克先生把它译成观念原则和实在原则，却只是把事情弄得更乱；他的实在原则已经在客体旁边设定了一个主体，§ 432 说这个主体“能推理，只是不能自在地思维，尽管各学派当然把两者当作一回事”。
在作为观念原则的理性旁边，在实在原则旁边，布特维克先生毕竟还特别需要感性，因为正如实在原则如此糟糕地成为理性的根据，以致人们在实在原则之外还需要一个理性，它大概也不会更好地成为感性的根据；关于这一点，人们要到后面才找到说明。
这种先验哲学的最后一部分——论先验的放弃，它从这一点开始：我们用尽一切哲学活动也无法超出观念原则与实在原则的思辨对立——列举出在一切哲学活动之后还剩下的谜；a) 意识对它自己就是一个解不开的谜；b) 感性表象的多重和杂多，既没有通过观念原则也没有通过实在原则得到解释；后者给出的只是一般客体，而不是这个或那个客体，§ 446。

前者，§ 447，是思维中的我，作为与杂多相对立的单纯者；所以我们为了解释杂多需要感性，§ 448。c) 就认识的形式和康德的表象规律而言，§ 451 除了让它们干脆搁在一边之外，没有剩下任何办法。——在理性这种先验满足的不可能面前，绝对真理只是一个观念，并且（§ 453）“在意识到不可能找到它被实现的情况下，我们就只好在经验上满足于经验真理或心理学真理的概念，我们——把这个概念思考为我们的表象与其对象的符合！！”
Satis superque. ——最后还跟着康德对理性心理学、宇宙论和神学的了断；在关于上帝的观念那里，§ 462，布特维克先生又只看出下面这一点的二律背反性质：实在性与观念性之间的对立持续存在，以及它通过纯粹思想而被消灭；却没有看出，一切与无的综合必须是绝对实在性。

en: The highest thing in this philosophy is consciousness; in it one finds, one knows not why, an ideal and a real principle, a sensibility, and a great many other things besides.
This consciousness is exactly the same substratum for everything as the soul-thing formerly was; the difference is purely formal, and philosophy has to regard it as nothing at all.
zh: 这种哲学的最高者就是意识；在意识里，人们不知道为什么就找到一个观念原则和一个实在原则、一个感性，还有一大堆别的东西。
这个意识和从前的灵魂物一样，恰恰是同一个为一切东西的基底；区别纯粹是形式上的，哲学必须把它看作完全不算什么。

en: It is clear from all the foregoing that the author, in his need to have a textbook of speculative philosophy, recognized very well the incoherence of the materials - especially the Kantian ones - but with regard to the principle of philosophy did not press through beyond the principle of the Kantian system, not beyond the idea of the absolute to the absolute itself - being or activity, these forms become indifferent even on the highest standpoint of speculation - and with regard to the materials, because the highest standpoint is not reached, could not construct them, but covered their nakedness with the expedient that the sceptic would have nothing to object to them in this poverty, and, given the little interest to be taken in them, was not precise with the definitions either with regard to correct distinctions or still less with regard to depth.
The various materials taken up make the whole into a mixture of very heterogeneous elements, of empirical psychology, ordinary logic, scepticism, Kantian criticism, and also transcendental idealism.

The latter, namely, sometimes supplies the beginnings of the sections; on account of the sceptical method the author does not want to begin with definitions, but the concept of what is to be defined is supposed - according to the demand of idealism - to produce itself through self-active thinking and through attention to it; but then it also remains with this demand, and there does not follow, as one would expect, a construction of the activities in their necessity, but rather there begins an analytical defining and narrating of what, as Kant and others assure us, is found in consciousness, as we saw above with the categories, that they are taken up in this way because Kant has them in this number; it is the same with the rest.

Such an eclecticism becomes original simply through itself, since the thread along which the parts of the alien systems run on is arbitrary and the forms of reflection in which the highest oppositions of dualism can be set up are infinite. - The fear of reason and of philosophy legitimates itself by this, that the reality of cognitions must first be properly grounded before one philosophizes; like Reinhold, it calls itself pure love of and faith in truth, or shyness before dogmatism, critical philosophizing, sceptical method; because one does not philosophize and yet something philosophical is to be done, in our times the invention of a provisional philosophizing has been made and the history of philosophy has been enriched with this new phenomenon.
zh: 从前面所说的全部可以看出：作者在需要有一本思辨哲学教科书的时候，把那些材料——尤其是康德的材料——的支离破碎看得很清楚，但在哲学的原则方面，他并没有穿透到康德体系的原则之外，没有越过绝对者的观念而达到绝对者本身——存在或活动，这些形式在思辨的最高立场上本身也变得无关紧要——；在材料方面，由于最高的立场没有达到，他不能建构这些材料，而是用这样一个应急办法遮盖它们的赤裸：怀疑论者在这种贫乏状态面前没有什么可反对的；并且由于人们对这些材料没有多少兴趣，他在定义上无论就正确的区分而言，还是更谈不上就深度而言，都没有做到精确。
所采纳的各式材料使整体变成了一个混合体，由极其异质的要素组成：经验心理学、通常的逻辑学、怀疑论、康德的批判论，还有先验观念论。

后者偶尔提供了各节的开始；由于怀疑论的方法，作者不想从定义开始，而是要下定义的东西的概念应当——按照观念论的要求——通过自己活动着的思维和对此的注意自行产生出来；可是事情也就停在这个要求上，接着并没有像可以期待的那样出现诸活动在其必然性中的建构，而是开始了一场分析式的下定义和叙述，叙述那些据康德和其他人保证存在于意识中的东西，就像我们上面在范畴那里看到的：它们被这样采纳，是因为康德正好有这么多范畴；其余的东西情形也一样。

这样一种折中主义单凭它自己就已经是独创的了，因为那些异己体系的各个部分所沿着延伸的那条线索是任意的，而二元论的最高对立可以在其中被建立起来的反思形式又是无限多的。——对理性和哲学的畏惧是这样为自己辩护的：在人们从事哲学之前，认识的实在性必须先得到妥当的论证；这种畏惧像在赖因霍尔德那里一样，自称对真理的纯粹的爱和信仰，或者自称对独断论的畏避、批判的哲学活动、怀疑论的方法；因为人们并不从事哲学，却又该做点哲学的事情，所以在我们这个时代就发明了一种临时的哲学活动，哲学史也因为这一新现象而变得更丰富了。

en: I. Brief scientific exposition of the untenability [and groundlessness] both of the transcendental-ideal[istic] system of Fichte and of the system of the vain doctrine of enjoyment [of his antipodes] and of the critical system, by J. Fr.
C. Werneburg, 1800.
zh: I. 关于费希特的先验观念[论]体系、[他的对跖者]的虚荣享乐说体系以及批判体系的不可持存[和无根据]的简短科学阐述，由 J. Fr.
C. 韦内堡，1800 年。

en: II.

Attempted brief, comprehensible preliminary portrayal of the all-science doctrine or the sole so-called philosophy, and a more comprehensible presentation of the groundlessness of both extreme systems, of idealism and of dogmatism, etc., by J. Fr.
C. Werneburg.
Publishing house for the most recent literature 1060 (1800).
zh: II.
对全知识学或唯一的所谓哲学所作的尝试性、简短、易懂的预先描述，以及对观念论和独断论这两个极端体系之无根据所作的更易懂的阐述等等，由 J. Fr.
C. 韦内堡。
最新文学出版书局 1060（1800）。

en: To the second writing, besides the title abbreviated here, yet another, more extensive title is added to excess, and the page numbers given are also to be understood according to the Taun system91). - It is precisely this dreary subjectivity that speaks in the content of the two pamphlets, which attain to no objective presentation, any more than to scientific views, but drifts about in general declamations of one and the same content and in hints that are supposed to be deep, and in a confusion that finds no thread, while at the same time making very great pretensions.

In the preface to Nr. I the author says that: most of the divided philosophical parties hope altogether for a man who not only possesses thorough philosophy but also unites philosophical mathematics with it - and appears as arbiter; he (W.) now presumes to show to both parties impartially, according to his powers, their errors; he feels thereby more than too much the importance and burden of such an office assumed on his own authority, and merely the hope that etc.
zh: 第二篇著作除了这里缩写的标题之外，还多余地附上了另一个更冗长的标题，而所给出的页码也要按照 Taun 体系91)来理解。——在这两本小册子的内容里说话的，正是这种凄惨的主体性：这两本小册子既达不到任何客观的表述，也达不到科学的见解，而是在同一个内容的泛泛空谈和故作深刻的暗示中、在一种找不到线索的混乱中打转，同时又提出极大的要求。
在 Nr. I 的序言里，作者说：分裂开来的哲学派别中大多数都一致盼望一个人，这人不只是拥有扎实的哲学，还把哲学性的数学与它结合起来——并作为仲裁者出场；他（韦内堡）现在敢于按自己的力量，不偏不倚地向双方指出他们的错误；他为此对这样一个擅自承担起来的职位的重要和沉重感受得过深，而只有那点希望，即等等。

en: In I., while the author wants to prove the groundlessness of the Fichtean system, he has regard to the Doctrine of Science and therewith to his (W.'s) friend Heusinger, who pained him (W.) very much with his writing against Fichte92); in II., to the presentation of the Doctrine of Science in the Philosophical Journal93).

We give the author's main principle, p. 19, in his own words, and therewith at the same time a sample of his style and manner: "The philosopher can and should abstract relatively, in a respect (yet by no means absolutely, unconditionally), i.e. stand off and abstract from something; that is, he should, through the freedom and necessity of perceiving and thinking, judge, separate, what is primordially united in perception and experience, in consciousness.

And he can and should, in turn, after and during the abstraction (standing off and abstracting), through the freedom and necessity of perceiving, primordially unite, conjoin, the primordially divided.

In perception and experience, the thing (the Thou), the primordially necessary, that which is to be and is determined independently of our freedom and according to which our cognition is to direct itself, and the intelligence, the spirit (the I), the primordially free, that which is to cognize, are inseparably bound together, i.e. these two primordial judgments, primordially divided things, are in a whole not merely united, but primordially united."

The procedure that imagines [it abstracts] from the Thou is idealism, - that which imagines it has abstracted entirely from the I, dogmatism; the procedure that commits no such violation on the sanctuary, the primordially united, is said to be naturalism; the primordially united the author calls I-Thou. - Apart from the above passage, in which the author's main thought is expressed, the rest of the two writings is a monotonous, hypochondriacal, apostrophizing opposing of idealism and dogmatism, a recurring declaiming etc., about which nothing further can be said, and in which the reviewer has come upon only one more bright passage, p. 41: "Man as a rational being first finds and recognizes his true dignity when he recognizes himself, as it were, as the mirror in which the infinite first recognizes and can recognize itself ...

He is the organ through which the infinite synthesis first becomes conscious of itself and intuits itself." - The author's fundamental idea cannot be denied the possibility that the idea of philosophy is expressed in it; but whether this is truly so is only recognizable, just as it has value and merit for me, when it is made scientific.
zh: 在第一部分里，作者为证明费希特体系没有根据，顾及《知识学》，并且由此顾及他（W.）的朋友海辛格，此人用他那篇反对费希特的文章92)让（W.）十分痛心；在第二部分里，则顾及《哲学杂志》93)上对知识学的阐述。
我们把作者第 19 页上的主要原则用他自己的话给出，同时也借此给出一个关于他文风和作风的样本：“哲学家能够而且应当相对地、有顾及地（然而绝不是绝对地、无条件地）作抽象，也就是说，从某物抽身并撇开；这就是说，他应当凭知觉和思维的自由与必然性，去判断、去分开那在知觉和经验中、在意识中原初地统一起来的东西。
而他又能够而且应当在抽象（抽身和撇开）之后并在此之中，凭知觉的自由与必然性，把原初被分开的东西原初地统一起来、联合起来。
在知觉和经验中，物（你）、原初必然者，即应当并且确实不依赖于我们的自由而被规定、我们的认识应当依照它来定向的东西，和智性、精神（我）、原初自由者，即应当去认识的东西，不可分割地结合在一起，也就是说，这两个原初判断、原初被分开的东西在一个整体中不只是被统一起来，而是被原初地统一起来。”

那种以为自己是从你来抽象的作法，是观念论；那种以为自己已经完全从自我抽象出来的作法，是独断论；而那种不在神圣之物、原初统一者身上犯下这种侵害的作法，据说就是自然主义；作者把原初统一者称为我—你。——除了上面这段表达了作者主要思想的地方，两篇著作中其余部分都是一种单调的、疑病的、呼告式的对观念论和独断论的对立，反复出现的慷慨陈词等等，对此再也说不出什么，而书评人在其中只还碰上一处明亮的地方，第 41 页：“人作为理性存在者，如今才第一次找到并认识到自己真正的尊严，因为他把自己仿佛认作那面镜子，无限者在那面镜子里才第一次认识到并且能够认识自己……
他是那个器官，无限的综合通过它才第一次意识到自己并直观到自身。”——不能否认作者的基本观念中含有这种可能：哲学的观念在它里面得到了表达；但这是否真的如此，只有在这观念被科学地做成时才能认出来，也只有在做成时它才对我有价值和功劳。

18.en: [Gerstäcker's Deduction of the Concept of Right]94)
18.zh: [格斯泰克尔的权利概念演绎]94)

en: Attempt at a commonly intelligible deduction of the concept of right from the highest grounds of knowledge, as a foundation for a future system of the philosophy of right.
By K. Fr.
Wilh.
Gerstäcker, Rechtskons. at Leipzig. Breslau, at Aug.
Schall 1801.
zh: 《从知识的最高根据出发对权利概念作通俗演绎的尝试，作为未来权利哲学体系的基础》
K. Fr. 著
Wilh.
格斯泰克尔，莱比锡的法律顾问（Rechtskons.）。布雷斯劳，奥古斯特·

en: The author has set himself a difficult task, to unite the deduction from the highest grounds of knowledge with common intelligibility; what is ordinarily the case in such an attempt, that common intelligibility gains the upper hand over the height of the grounds, is also found in this attempt.
zh: 作者给自己出了一道难题：把从知识的最高根据出发的演绎同通俗易懂结合起来；这种尝试里通常会出现的情形——通俗易懂压过根据的高度而占了上风——在这篇尝试里同样可以看到。

en: The introduction contains distinctions, supposed to be deep, of metaphysics and physics of right; metaphysics is to separate the idea of right from the concepts so often exchanged for it, morality, happiness and arbitrary force (the right of the stronger), as well as from all particular empirical relations in which it could express itself, to develop with completeness the characteristics contained in it, to derive from these a system of pure fundamental propositions of reason about right, etc. - Natural law (the physics of right) is to refer the idea set up by metaphysics, as well as the system of pure principles of reason derived from it, to the whole circle of possible human relations that belong under it and require the examination whether and in how far they are determined by the law of right. - This separating of the purely formal concept of right from its reality turns the metaphysics of right into a mere formalism that would have to do only with an empty concept and its analysis, and the physics of right into a subsuming of possible human relations under the general concept set up in the former so-called metaphysics; but these possible human relations, to which the concept that does not dwell in them and is set up separately is first applied in physics - how then does such a procedure come to them other than in an empirical way? for they do not lie in the concept; and that concept, what is it other than the product of an abstracting formalism? - This whole distinction of the science of right into metaphysics and physics expresses nothing but the common method of the sciences, which take their content from common experience and their form from reflection; the last grounds of knowledge, from which right is in such a way to be deduced for us, can so little be the last that they do not rise to philosophy at all.
zh: 导论里包含一些应当很深刻的、关于权利的形而上学与物理学的区分；形而上学要把权利的观念同那些屡屡被拿来同它互换的概念——道德、幸福和任意的暴力（强者的权利）——分开，也要把它从一切特殊的经验关系（它可能在这些关系中表现出来）分开，完整地展开其中包含的标志，再从这些标志引出一个关于权利的纯粹理性根本命题的体系，等等。——自然法（权利的物理学）则要把形而上学所设定的观念，以及由它引出的纯粹理性原则的体系，联系到可能的人类关系的整个范围上，这些关系归属于它，并且需要检验它们是否以及在多大程度上由权利法则所规定。——把纯形式的权利概念同它的实在性这样分开，就把权利的形而上学变成一种单纯的形式主义，它只和一个空洞的概念及其分析打交道，而把权利的物理学变成把可能的人类关系归摄到前一种所谓的形而上学所设定的一般概念之下；但是这些可能的人类关系——那个并不内在于它们、而是被单独设定的概念在物理学中才被应用于它们——，这样一种做法除了以经验的方式，又怎么能达到它们呢？因为它们并不在概念里；而那个概念，它除了是一种进行抽象的形式主义的产物，还能是什么？——把权利的科学这样整个地区分为形而上学和物理学，所表达的不过是各门科学通常的方法：它们从普通经验中取内容，从反思中取形式；那些据说以这种方式为我们演绎出权利的知识的最后根据，根本算不上是最后的，它们压根儿升不到哲学。

en: The author then divides his treatise into three parts; the first is to grasp, from manifold utterances of common sense about legal relations, the components of the concept that hovers darkly before it from right and to unite them into a general concept, - the second is to ascend to the highest grounds of knowledge and from these too to derive the necessity (reality) of right, and consequently at the same time the extent and the characteristics of its concept, while the third is to compare the concept found at this height with that from which the investigation started, and for every component taken up into the latter to conduct the proof from the former.
zh: 接着，作者把自己的论文分成三个部分；第一部分应当从普通常识关于权利关系的种种说法中，把握那个在常识面前关于权利隐隐浮现的概念的各个组成部分，并把它们结合成一个一般概念；第二部分应当上升到知识的最高根据，也从这些根据引出权利的必然性（实在性），从而同时引出它的概念的范围和标志；第三部分则应当把在这个高度上找到的概念同研究由之出发的那个东西加以比较，并为后一个概念所收纳的每一个组成部分，从前一个概念出发作出证明。

en: As for the development of the concept of right out of judgments of common sense, according to the same author the pronouncements of common sense about right differ from knowledge about it in that common sense is in complete unconsciousness about the idea (formal fundamental propositions and concepts it indeed has, but in the case at hand it itself directly made the restrictions of its general concepts, which knowledge must already contain) as it is about the connection of the totality of legal relations, and only in the individual case, according to the whole of an intuition, pronounces its It is right or wrong.

The judgments of common sense about right and wrong can therefore be presented only through a multitude of examples of actual cases, a multitude that may not be gathered together in an indeterminate way, but must be selected according to the idea of totality in such an extent that the extent of legal relations would be exhausted in them, which is already impossible in and for itself and also because common sense is common sense precisely for the reason that in its living judgments it does not abstract and passes no pure judgment about what is legal, but mixes in the consideration of the ethical.

G. did not choose this way, but sought to overhear from common sense the general concept of its judging about right, which means nothing other than that he actually does not let the judging of common sense come to words at all, but in taking it up immediately explains it, i.e. sets forth nothing but his own concepts; thus, for example, it is set forth as a judging of common sense: that an action by which a violent effect is produced in the free sphere of activity of a human being is held to be unlawful, its author must have known this violent coincidence of his deed with the external freedom of the one restricted, or must at least have had the obligation to concern himself about it, etc.
zh: 至于从普通常识的判断出发发展权利概念这件事，按照作者本人的说法，普通常识关于权利的论断之所以区别于关于权利的知识，是因为常识对观念处于完全的无意识之中（形式上的根本命题和概念它当然有，但在眼前这个场合，是它自己直接给自己的那些一般概念加上了限制，而这些限制知识必须已经包含在内），对权利关系的总体性的联系也同样无意识，并且只在个别场合，依照一个直观的整体，说出它那句“这是对的或不对的”。
因此，普通常识关于权利与不义的判断，只能通过大量现实事例的例子来展示，而这一大堆例子不可以不确定地随手抓来，必须依照总体性的观念，以这样的范围来挑选，使权利关系的范围在其中被穷尽；这本身就已经是不可能的，而且也因为：普通常识之所以是普通常识，正是由于它在自己活生生的判断里不作抽象，对权利的东西不下纯粹判断，而是把对伦理的东西的考虑掺和进来。

G. 没有选这条路，而是设法从普通常识那里偷听来它作权利判断的一般概念，这无非是说：他其实根本不让普通常识的判断说话，而是一面把它接过来，一面立刻解说它，也就是说，讲出来的无非是他自己的概念；例如，作为普通常识的一种判断被端出来的是：一种行为，如果以暴力介入一个人的自由活动范围，就被看作违法的，那么它的作者必定知道自己的行为同被限制者的外在自由的这种暴力性碰撞，或者至少必定有义务去操心这件事，等等。

en: The second section, p. 25, which contains the deduction of the concept of right from the highest grounds of knowledge, at once gives strange representations about the concept of scientific deduction; the author says, p. 26: If the concept of right had its object in intuition, one would only need to hold it together with this in order to be convinced of its truth, as is the case with the concepts and propositions of "pure mathematics and empirical natural science.

The correctness or incorrectness of these must immediately become evident from the comparison undertaken between them and intuition, without one having need, after the agreement of both has been found, to seek other grounds."

For the existence of intuition no one who has senses could deny, - and the harmony of a concept and proposition with it no one who possesses common judgment; a proposition agreeing with the appearances in all points therefore has complete evidence. - That would thus be the manner in which Pythagoras would have proved the proposition that the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the squares of the two legs, - that he would have tried it out in the appearances, how his proposition thereby agrees with them.
In what the author calls empirical natural science, this is indeed the procedure, but for that very reason it is empirical knowledge and not science.

Without doubt the author has been led to such concepts of scientific construction by misunderstanding what Kant says in the introduction to the Critique of Pure Reason [B 14 ff.] about the a priori character of the judgments of mathematics and natural science, and in what respect their necessity is grounded on intuition.
zh: 第二部分，第 25 页，包含从知识的最高根据出发对权利概念的演绎，它一上来就给出了关于科学演绎这一概念的一些古怪表象；作者在第 26 页说：如果权利概念在直观中有自己的对象，那么人们只需把它同这直观放在一起比照，就会确信它的真理，就像“纯粹数学和经验自然科学的概念和命题的情形那样。
这些东西的正确或不正确，必定立刻从它们与直观之间所作的比照中显露出来，人无须在发现两者一致之后再去寻找别的根据。”
因为直观的存在，凡有感官的人都不能否认；而一个概念和命题与直观的和谐，凡具有普通判断力的人也不能否认；所以，一个在一切点上同现象都一致的命题，就具有完全的明证性。——那么这就会是毕达哥拉斯证明“斜边的平方等于两条直角边的平方”这一命题的方式了，——他会在现象里试一试，他的命题怎样同这些现象相合。
在作者称为经验自然科学的东西里，做法当然是这样，但正因如此，它是经验而不是科学。
毫无疑问，作者之所以被引向这样一些关于科学建构的概念，是因为他误解了康德在《纯粹理性批判》导论里[B 14 ff.]关于数学和自然科学判断的先验性、以及它们的必然性在何种程度上以直观为根据所说的话。

en: With the deduction of right itself, which the author wants to pump up from the highest grounds of knowledge, right out of the deepest depths of reason, he takes a very wide start; on p. 29 the author begins it with this: that if he surveys the whole horizon of knowledge possible for him, it divides into two regions that completely fill it, into the inner and the outer. - The outer world and the inner world are then likewise overheard as to what is found in them, just as common sense was in the first section.

For many pages it is recounted that, if one had never tasted sour things or seen a purple coat, one would also not know what sour etc. is; but precisely from the fact that everyone must sense these properties, it follows that they are nothing on outer things. 'The more I think about it, the more evident it becomes to me that colours and consequently shapes, also space and time, are nothing on the things themselves but merely sensations in me, are simple, indivisible occurrences of my spirit, which I first spread out upon something outside me; all are compelled states in me, for after separating off all properties that are obviously only sensations, nothing more remains on the things.' - This highest idealism is therefore grounded solely on this, that attention is drawn to how everything objective is something subjective, - the smellable and tasteable is in smelling and tasting; a truth that probably no realist has yet doubted, for whose sake it is unnecessary to evoke idealism, for it is at home in empirical psychology. - 'The shapes are compelled actions of my spirit; if I cancel the visible manifold and its composite, nothing remains but the outer force, an efficacy that compels my inner being in a determinate way, that produces a check in the free activity of my spirit; but I am therefore not to hold the assumption of outer forces for a phantom, nor all the outer for a mere aggregate of my states and of their forced connection; I would otherwise have to deny, against my better conviction, the compulsion grounded in the deepest depth of my essence, to have to presuppose something independent of a sensing and connecting and underlying it; the thing in itself, because the feeling of necessity is after all present only in myself, is nothing but an unknown something, the absolute impulse that I posit in order to explain my sensing, a necessary presupposition, and its constitution is not to be discovered in experience; that I represent to myself the unknown ground of my sensing as activities, as forces - by this I do not mean to presume to know its inner essence, but the motive is to have, for my inquiring reason, an answer to the question about the condition of the necessity of sensing and outer relating.' - (But how can inquiring reason find itself satisfied there, where it does not know the inner essence? does it then inquire only after the cognition of the outer?
Is rational cognition then anything other than cognition of the inner essence of things? of things as they are in themselves?)
zh: 至于权利本身的演绎——作者想把它从知识的最高根据，真从理性最深的深处抽上来——，他起手拉得很远；在第 29 页上，作者是这样开头的：如果他环顾对自己来说可能的知识的整个地平线，这地平线就分成两个把它完全填满的区域，即内在的东西和外在的东西。——然后，外在世界和内在世界也照样被偷听，看里面有什么，就像第一部分里对普通常识所做的那样。

一连好多页都在讲：如果人从没尝过酸的东西、没见过紫色的外套，他也就不知道酸等等是什么；但正因为每个人都必定感觉到这些属性，它们就不在外部事物上。“我越是思考这件事，就越是明白：颜色、因而还有形状，以及空间和时间，都不是事物本身上的东西，而只是我里面的感觉，是我精神的简单的、不可分的发生，我先把它们铺展到我外面的某个东西上；一切都是我里面被逼出来的状态，因为把一切显然只是感觉的属性分离掉之后，事物上就再也不剩什么了。”——所以，这种最高的观念论仅仅依据于这一点：让人注意到，一切客观的东西都是主观的东西，——可嗅的和可尝的东西就在嗅和尝之中；这是一个大概还没有哪个实在论者怀疑过的真理，为了它根本不必去唤起观念论，因为它在经验心理学里本来就有家。——“形状是我精神被逼出来的行动；如果我把可见的杂多及其组合取消掉，剩下的就只有外在的力，一种以确定的方式强迫我的内在、在我的精神的自由活动中造成阻碍的作用；但我并不因此就把对外在的力的假定当作幻象，也不把一切外在的东西当作我的状态及其被逼出来的联结的单纯总合；否则我就得违背自己更好的确信，否认那种植根于我本质最深处、要我必须预设某种不依赖于感觉和联结并作为其基础的东西的强制；自在之物，因为必然性的感觉毕竟只在我自己里面才有，所以无非是一个未知的某物，是我为了解释我的感觉而设定的绝对阻抗，一个必要的预设，而它的性质在经验里是发现不了的；我把我的感觉的那个未知根据表象为活动、表象为力，我并不是借此妄称认识它的内在本质，而只是要为我进行探究的理性，对感觉和外在关联的必然性的条件这一问题有一个答案。”——（但进行探究的理性在它不认识内在本质的地方，怎么能对自己感到满意呢？它难道只探究外在东西的认识吗？
难道理性认识是别的什么，而不是对事物内在本质的认识吗？不是对事物自在所是的样子的认识吗？）

en: The investigation finally comes to a standstill where it reaches the highest grounds of knowledge, p. 118. 'These are the two infinites, the free I and the outer forces; how then do these two infinites hang together, is the one the product of the other?
These questions are absolutely unanswerable; - for in every consciousness, and hence also in that of any possible answerer, both must occur as antipodal.
Through their constant coming together, through their never-ending struggle from opposed points, there first arises actuality, experience, knowledge, cognition.

Both must remain eternally incompatible, each of the opposed is something absolute for itself, and yet each is also conditioned by the other.' - And these are then the highest grounds of knowledge, which, as we see, consist in nothing other than the most ordinary and most formal dualism, glossed over with Fichtean colours and duly edifying and rhetorical amplifications.
zh: 研究最终停下来的地方，就是它达到知识的最高根据之处，见第 118 页。“这就是两个无限者，自由的我与外在的力；这两个无限者究竟怎样联系在一起，一个是另一个的产物吗？
这些问题绝对无法回答；——因为在每一个意识里，因而也在任何一个可能的回答者的意识里，两者都必定作为对跖的东西出现。
正是通过它们不断的相遇，通过它们从对立各点出发的永不停息的斗争，才产生出现实性、经验、知识、认识。
两者必须永远不可统一，对立的两项中每一项都自为地是绝对者，而每一项又都通过另一项而受到制约。”——而这就是知识的最高根据，如我们所看到的，它们不外乎是最寻常、最形式化的二元论，只是用费希特式的色彩和恰如其分的教化腔与修辞铺张涂抹了一层。

en: The relation of lawful freedom is now introduced in such a way that the human being, through his body and the outer world, stands in the relation of possible reciprocal effects with the free beings of his species, whereby the one can oppose irresistible coercion to the efficacy of the other; the condition in which neither their efficacy is violently checked [is], nor do they check the same among one another, is that relation of lawful freedom. - There now follows still more about the moral law, which one cannot call anything but declamations; and neither the highest grounds of knowledge nor a deduction of right from them are anywhere to be seen, but nothing but Kantian moral philosophy and words of the Fichtean idealism taken as a dualism, presented with empty declamatory sweep, which is probably supposed to make the matter popular and generally comprehensible.
zh: 权利性的自由这一关系现在是这样引出的：人通过自己的身体和外部世界，与自己的族类中那些自由的存在者处于可能交互作用的关系之中，因此一方能够对另一方的活动施加不可抗拒的强制；而那种既没有任何一方的活动受到暴力阻碍、它们彼此也不阻碍这种活动的状态，就是权利性的自由这一关系。——接着还讲了不少关于道德法则的话，这些只能叫做慷慨陈词；无论在哪儿都看不到知识的最高根据，也看不到从这些根据出发对权利作出的演绎，看到的只不过是康德道德哲学和费希特观念论的一些话被当成一种二元论，用空洞的慷慨激昂的腔调讲出来，大概是想把这事情弄得通俗易懂。

en: The third section, p. 154, the proof of the correctness of the concept developed in the first section out of judgements of common understanding, is of course found very easily; for in the first section the concepts of the second were already explained into common understanding, and the whole could therefore just as well have been treated under the title of the first section.
zh: 第三节，第 154 页，即对第一节从健全知性的判断中发展出来的那个概念的正确性的证明，自然很容易就找到了；因为在第一节里，第二节的那些概念早已被解释进健全知性之中，所以整个东西本来也完全可以放在第一节的标题下处理。
